segments.name: Transaction-based revenues
segments.note: Fees from trading: options $399M (+31%), event contracts $173M (up 6x), equities $121M (+41%), partly offset by crypto $120M (−55%).

segments.name: Net interest revenues
segments.note: Interest earned on customer cash, margin loans and securities lending, minus interest paid — down as rates fell and securities lending slowed.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Robinhood Gold subscriptions and new services such as Trump Accounts — the fastest-growing slice.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building and running the app and trading platform — the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Operations
opex.note: Day-to-day operations and customer support — up 139% YoY as new businesses like Trump Accounts launch.

opex.name: Provision for credit losses
opex.note: Money set aside for cardholders who may not repay — up 173% YoY as the Gold Card loan book grows.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and growth spending to win new funded accounts.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — down 12% YoY.

verdict: Robinhood's revenue rose 12% to $1.42B as event contracts exploded and options trading jumped 31% — but profit fell 14%, because credit-loss provisions nearly tripled on its growing card business and interest revenue shrank.
footerNote: Robinhood does not report a separate cost of revenue; 'Brokerage and transaction' — the direct cost of executing customers' trades — is shown as the direct cost here. Net income of $476M includes $8M attributable to non-controlling interests; $468M (EPS $0.51) is attributable to Robinhood.

takeaways.title: Event contracts are a real business now
takeaways.text: Event-contract revenue hit $173M, up more than 6x in a year, alongside options revenue of $399M (+31%) — prediction markets went from experiment to a top-three revenue line.

takeaways.title: Credit losses are the watch item
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses nearly tripled to $71M as the Gold Card loan book grows. It is the cost of becoming a lender — fine while defaults stay low, painful if they don't.

takeaways.title: Interest revenue is fading as rates fall
takeaways.text: Net interest revenue fell 9% to $415M on lower short-term rates and weaker securities lending — a reminder that a big slice of Robinhood's income depends on the Fed, not just on traders.

follow100Note: Kept-as-profit includes −$4.21 of other expense per $100 of revenue; the rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.
